# Phase 164.6.3: CIDOCSPATH — a docs-only PR stops running the code gates, and a code PR is proven to still run every one of them - Context

**Gathered:** 2026-09-12
**Status:** Ready for planning
**Mode:** Auto-generated (autonomous smart-discuss; infrastructure phase — decisions were already locked in the ROADMAP entry and are restated here with the measurements that constrain them)

<domain>
## Phase Boundary

Change **WHEN** the CI gate corpus is invoked, and nothing else. A pull request whose diff
touches only pure-docs paths stops running the code-gate jobs; a pull request that touches any
code path still runs every single one of them.

⛔ NOT in scope: changing which gates exist, what any gate asserts, or the contents of any gate.
⛔ NOT in scope: the `push: branches: [main]` trigger — see the decision below.

</domain>

<decisions>
## Implementation Decisions

### Mechanism — job-level `if:`, never workflow-level `paths-ignore`

- **A `changes` detector job emits a boolean, and the code-gate jobs carry a job-level `if:` on
  it.** The ROADMAP already rules that "a job-level `if:` on a changed-files step is usually
  safer than workflow-level `paths-ignore`". Scouting confirms it is not merely safer here, it
  is the only correct option — see the always-on list below.
- ⛔ **Workflow-level `paths-ignore` is REJECTED, on evidence, not on taste.** It is
  all-or-nothing: it would also suppress `plan-anchor-verify`, which exists *specifically* to
  re-resolve the anchors a pending `PLAN.md` asserts, and a `.planning/**`-only PR is precisely
  the PR that adds or moves those anchors. It would also suppress `secret-scan` on a PUBLIC
  repo. Skipping either is a REGRESSION wearing an optimisation's clothes.
- The detector must be a real job whose classification is readable in the run log, not an
  inline expression duplicated across twenty `if:` lines.

### The always-on set (runs on EVERY PR, docs-only included)

Measured from `.github/workflows/ci.yml` at `eab976bb`:

- **`plan-anchor-verify`** — its whole subject is `.planning/**`. `if: github.event_name ==
  'pull_request'`, strict row in the aggregator. It MUST NOT gain a docs-only skip.
- **`secret-scan`** — the repo is PUBLIC and `.planning/` is TRACKED; a planning document is a
  perfectly good place to leak a key.
- **`version-gate`** — already exempts planning-only PRs from INSIDE
  `scripts/check-version-bump.mjs` ("Planning-only PRs are EXEMPT by design"). Adding an outer
  path filter would put two exemption mechanisms on one gate, which is the divergence class this
  repo already books defects for. Leave it alone.
- **`docs-link-check`** — cheap, and it is a docs gate. No reason to suppress it on a docs PR.

Everything else is a candidate for the filter. That is the 21-job corpus minus these four.

### The aggregator — ONE uniform arm, never a per-row tolerance

- ⭐ **The `frontend` aggregator is the whole hazard and it is NOT the hazard the ROADMAP names.**
  The ROADMAP warns about a required check reporting *pending forever*. Measured 2026-09-12:
  `gh api .../branches/main/protection` returns **404 Branch not protected** and
  `gh api .../rulesets` returns **[]**, so there is no required check to wedge today. The REAL
  failure is different and worse: the aggregator carries `if: always()` and its result loop's
  DEFAULT ARM sets `fail=1` on any non-`success`, `skipped` included. Filter the jobs and leave
  the loop alone and a docs-only PR turns the aggregator **RED**, not pending.
- **Therefore the loop learns exactly ONE new arm, driven by the same detector output, applied
  uniformly to every row that the filter is allowed to skip.** ⛔ NOT a per-row tolerance arm —
  the job headers forbid those by name for `frontend-seam-redis`, `sql-gate-lint`,
  `sql-mutation` and `frontend-local-stack`, and this phase must not smuggle one in through a
  side door.
- The detector's output is the single point of trust. If it misclassifies a code diff as
  docs-only, every gate greens at once. That is this phase's vacuity surface and it is where
  the anti-vacuity work goes.

### Anti-vacuity — what the phase closes on

- Per the milestone's standing doctrine: **neuter → observe RED → restore.** The control here is
  the detector. Neuter it so it reports docs-only on a diff that touches code, and the
  observation that must be recorded is a RED board, not a short one.
- ⭐ **Criterion 2 is the real criterion and it is satisfied by TWO REAL PRs, not a dry run.**
  One docs-only PR (diff entirely under `.planning/**`) and one code PR, both merged or at least
  both with a completed check board, both job sets enumerated with `gh run view --json jobs`.
- **The before/after job set is compared explicitly and every difference is named.** A code PR
  running fewer than the pre-change corpus is a REGRESSION and closes nothing.
- The shared-TEST mutex claim is measured by the ABSENCE of a `61616158` acquire in the
  docs-only PR's run — from the log, not from the job list.

### Trigger scope — `pull_request` only

- **The `push: branches: [main]` trigger is NOT filtered.** `ci.yml`'s own header records why:
  "every commit must produce its own recorded green CI run (deploy automation + branch
  protection key on per-SHA status)", and Railway waits on main CI and SKIPS the
  analytics-service deploy when it is red. A main commit with no run, or with a half-skipped
  run, is a change to deploy behaviour, which this phase is not allowed to make.
- Consequence, stated rather than discovered later: a docs-only change still pays the full
  corpus once, on the merge push. The win claimed by this phase is the PR-side run and the
  PR-side mutex acquire, and the SUMMARY must say so rather than claim the whole 3,001
  job-seconds.

### Claude's Discretion

- The exact detector implementation (`dorny/paths-filter` vs a pinned action vs a `git diff`
  step) — pick whatever is already pinned-by-SHA in this repo's idiom and needs no new secret.
- The exact spelling of the pure-docs path set beyond `.planning/**`.
- Whether the detector job is folded into an existing early job or stands alone.

</decisions>

<code_context>
## Existing Code Insights

### The corpus, measured at `eab976bb`

21 job keys in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: `deps-cache`, `frontend-typecheck`, `frontend-lint`,
`frontend-test`, `frontend-coverage`, `frontend-seam-redis`, `frontend-local-stack`,
`frontend-policy`, `knip`, `frontend-build`, `sql-gate-lint`, `sql-mutation`,
`plan-anchor-verify`, `frontend`, `sql-tests`, `secret-scan`, `version-gate`,
`docs-link-check`, `python`, `e2e`, `e2e-seeded`, `lighthouse-mobile`.

### The aggregator — `ci.yml:2193`

`needs:` 13 jobs, `if: always()`, then a shell loop over
`needs.<job>.result`. Three rows carry hand-written tolerance arms (`e2e-seeded`, `sql-tests`,
`plan-anchor-verify`); every other row takes the strict default `elif [ "$result" != "success" ]
; then fail=1`. Four job headers state in prose that their row must NEVER be given a tolerance
arm. Any filter that skips a strict-row job without teaching this loop reddens the board.

### The mutex

Advisory key `61616158` — 26 occurrences in `ci.yml`, 7 in `supabase-migrate.yml`. Taken by
`sql-tests` and `e2e-seeded`, both of which are aggregator rows. This is the coupling that makes
a roadmap typo delay other people's CI, and it is the phase's stated motivation.

### Integration points

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — the only file that must change for the mechanism.
- `src/__tests__/` — where the anti-vacuity assertion about the detector's classification will
  live, alongside `mutation-runner-floors.test.ts` and the other ratchet tests.

</code_context>
